The travel issue, part two

Excuse me, there’s a problem

Your last lesson before the trip. Today: the words for a hotel and a restaurant, what to say when something is wrong, and a small new piece of grammar: I’ll, for the moment you decide, offer or promise.

The air conditioning isn’t working, the bill is wrong, and Lu can’t come into the restaurant. No problem: I’ll call reception.

          5

          I’ll: decide, offer, promise

          One small word for the moment you decide, offer or promise something. Listen to the examples and repeat them.

          • Decide nowI’ll have…Are you ready to order? Yes. I’ll have the fish, please.
          • OfferI’ll… / Shall I…?Your bag looks heavy. I’ll carry it. Shall I open the window?
          • PromiseI’ll… / I won’t…I’ll call you back in five minutes. I won’t forget.

          The forms

          MeaningPatternExample
          yes, I decide / offer / promiseI’ll + verb (I’ll = I will)I’ll have the steak. We’ll take the room.
          no, I promise not towon’t + verb (won’t = will not)I won’t be late. She won’t bark.
          an offer as a questionShall I…?Shall I carry your bag? Shall I call a taxi?
          an idea for both of usShall we…?Shall we sit on the terrace?
          the other person promiseshe’ll / she’ll / they’llThe waiter says he’ll bring a bowl for Lu.

          I’ll or I’m going to?

          • I’m going to stay in a hotel near the sea. A plan. I decided before.
          • It’s hot in here. I’ll open the window. I decide now, at this moment.
          • Not I have the fish. Say I’ll have the fish.

          Listen and repeat

          • I’ll have the fish, please.
          • Shall I carry your bag?
          • I’ll call you back in five minutes.
          • Don’t worry, I won’t forget.

            Travel tips

            Staying in a hotel with your dog

            More and more hotels say “Dogs welcome!” But every hotel has its rules, so here are five tips.

            Ask first. Before you book, write or call: “Can I bring a small dog?” Some hotels take dogs only in a few rooms, and some ask for extra money, usually ten to twenty euros a night.

            Say it at reception. When you check in, tell them about your dog: “This is Lu. She’s very quiet.” Many hotels will give you a bowl, and some will give your dog a bed or a treat!

            In the room, don’t leave your dog alone for a long time. A dog in a new place can get nervous and bark, and the people in the next room won’t be happy.

            In the restaurant, ask: “Can my dog come in?” In many hotels the answer is no, but you can sit on the terrace, or you can order food to your room.

            One last tip: bring a towel from home. After a walk in the rain you’ll need it, and the hotel’s white towels are for people!

              8

              The sounds of ’ll and won’t

              I’ll is one short sound: /aɪl/. And won’t /wəʊnt/ is not want /wɒnt/. Listen and repeat.

              • I’ll /aɪl/
              • we’ll /wiːl/
              • it’ll /ˈɪtl/
              • won’t /wəʊnt/
              • want /wɒnt/
              • I have the fish. / I’ll have the fish.
              • We call reception. / We’ll call reception.
              • I want to go. / I won’t go.
              • It’ll be fine. She won’t bark, I promise.

                  Problems!

                  Eight things that can go wrong on a trip. Read the card and say what you’ll do and what you’ll say. Then open the card to compare.

                  • I’ll call reception.
                  • I’ll ask for…
                  • Excuse me, there’s a problem with…
                  • I asked for…, not…
                  • I think there’s a mistake.
                  11

                  Role-plays

                  Listen to each line and say it. Then play the scenes with your teacher.

                  1. YouHello, this is room six-one-three. There’s a problem with the air conditioning.
                  2. YouI’m sorry to bother you again. I can’t get a wi-fi signal.
                  3. ReceptionI’m sorry, madam. I’ll send somebody up right now.
                  4. YouA table for one, please. Can my dog come in?
                  5. YouI’ll have the chicken, please. And still water.
                  6. YouExcuse me, I asked for the chicken, and this is fish.
                  7. YouCan I have the bill, please? I think there’s a mistake.

                  Scene 1: calling reception

                  It’s your first evening in the hotel. Something in the room isn’t working. Call reception, say your room number, explain the problem and thank them. Then call again with a second problem.

                  Scene 2: dinner with Lu

                  You and Lu arrive at a restaurant. Ask for a table and ask about the dog. Order a starter, a main course and a drink. Then something is wrong: say it politely. At the end, ask for the bill.

                  On the trip

                  Only if you want: each day of the trip, say one sentence with I’ll in your head when you decide something (I’ll have the tea. I’ll take the ferry.). On 28 November, tell Alena the best one!
